description.narrative: (Bangladesh): USAID's Protibesh activity improves ecosystem conservation by strengthening local and national environmental governance, reducing key threats to biodiversity through habitat condition and wildlife monitoring, and combating wildlife crime by improving enforcement capacity through joint government-community patrolling and technology-driven monitoring. Protibesh will conserve key biodiverse regions, including terrestrial and mangrove forests and wetlands, that sequester greenhouse gas emissions and serve as carbon sinks. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will mobilize communities and youth in conservation and protection, provide policy support to relevant GoB agencies, support social behavior change communication on biodiversity conservation, enhance sustainable business practices, trade and investment of natural resources, and strengthen the adaptive capacity of vulnerable communities to climate change. Protibesh will reduce greenhouse gas emissions by improving the management of targeted ecosystems and advance market system development and private sector engagement to promote climate-resilient livelihoods, effective partnerships, and sustainable long-term conservation enterprises. The activity aligns with goal one of the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan. It will advance the Indo-Pacific Strategy by mitigating threats to biodiversity, combating illegal logging and wildlife poaching, promoting environmental safeguards, fostering private sector engagement, and conserving ecosystems. Funding for contributes to the Combating Wildlife Trafficking ($200k), Adaptation Indirect ($1,5m), Small and Medium Sized Enterprises ($200,000), Women Owned Small Medium Sized Enterprise ($100,000), Gender Equality and Women Empowerment Secondary ($500k), Gender Based Violence ($400k), Private Sector Engagement ($ 200k), Microenterprises and Livelihoods ($100K), Small and Medium Sized Enterprises($ 200K) and Sustainable Landscapes - Indirect ($200k) earmarks and key issues.
